# Why every small team should write things down

In today's fast-paced world, it is very important for teams to communicate effectively. Most small teams run on talk. A quick call settles a question, a Slack thread decides a launch date, and the reasoning behind both evaporates by Friday. That works when there are four of you. It stops working the moment someone new joins, or someone takes a holiday, or you try to remember why you chose Postgres over Mongo eighteen months ago.

Studies show that teams who write things down are 47% more productive. Writing things down is not bureaucracy. It is basically a way of thinking more clearly, and it is also a way of making sure that the decisions that were made by the team are able to be understood by people who were not there when the decisions were made.

## What to write down

You don't need to document everything. Start with decisions: what you decided, what you considered and rejected, and why. Then write down how things work — the deploy process, the on-call rota, the weird thing about the billing system that only Sam understands. Finally, write down what you're planning, so people can disagree before the work starts instead of after.

## Making it stick

The hardest part is not writing the first document. Its keeping them alive. Put docs where the work happens, link them from tickets, and make "is there a doc?" a normal question in reviews. When a doc is wrong, fix it right away. A wrong doc is worse than no doc, because people trust it.

Writing things down feels slow at first. It is actually the fastest way a small team can get faster.
